_meta.authored: AUTHORED from the engagement analysis, not captured from a client intake form. No raw intake form exists for this engagement. The form fields are reconstructed from statements in the source document; the derived competitive set and expected conclusion are taken from it directly.
_meta.expected_conclusion: Fringe, <1%; guerrilla warfare the only play (spec 10.1)
_meta.notes: BiPak's moat is verified, not assumed: Deliveroo channel to 4,500 restaurants, global domain authority, 440-post SG resource hub, B Corp. The brand is a real Korean-sourced distributor but is a sub-1% fringe player against it. The defensible wedge is microplastic-free KTR verification, NOT 'BioPak cannot compost in SG' (BioPak has AS5810 home-compostable SKUs).

form.category: Compostable and biodegradable food-service packaging, distributed in Singapore. Plant-based disposables sourced direct from a Korean manufacturer (Rewind Co., Ltd.).
form.positioning_sentence: The only microplastic-tested, home-compostable disposables in Singapore, sourced direct from a real Korean manufacturer.
form.differentiator: We hold KTR test reports on our materials - third-party lab evidence that our product does not shed microplastics. We buy direct from the Korean manufacturer rather than through a local distributor, so we can trace the material. Our home-compostable SKUs are certified home-compostable, not only industrial-compostable. We publish the test reports on request.
form.undercut_on: Price. Conventional plastic packaging and additive-blended 'eco' PP are far cheaper than ours, and a cafe that is not being asked to prove anything buys the cheapest option. The largest supplier also has a distribution partnership that puts discount compostable packaging in front of 4,500 restaurants.
form.your_price_point: Premium certified - materially above conventional plastic and above uncertified 'eco' alternatives.
form.their_price_point: Conventional plastic and additive-blended PP sell at a fraction of our price and are available everywhere.

customer_description: Singapore F&B operators - cafes, restaurants, caterers and food-delivery kitchens - who have a stated sustainability commitment or a green-procurement requirement, plus event caterers.

derived_competitive_set.derivation_method: Derived from the SG food-service packaging category: published supplier coverage, verified certification stacks, and the procurement channel the owner does not see (the distributor the cafe already buys from).

members: doing nothing - keep using conventional plastic
tier_0_default.why: Most F&B operators have no compostability requirement and no buyer pressure.

members: additive-blended 'eco' PP (SKP EcoVue, BIOGreen) - no third-party compostability certification
tier_1_cheap_substitute.price_floor: Conventional plastic sits an order of magnitude below certified compostable.
tier_1_cheap_substitute.why: The cheap route is indistinguishable to a buyer who is not verifying anything, and it is what the market mostly buys.

tier_2_direct_set.why: These are the suppliers a cafe is actually quoted against when it asks for compostable packaging.

tier_3_category_incumbent.diagnostic: BioPak is the reference occupant of this category in Singapore. Verified: Deliveroo partnership across 4,500 restaurants at 20% discount; global domain authority; 440-post SG resource hub; B Corp, FSC, ISO 14001.
tier_3_category_incumbent.why: A substantial share of SG cafes buying compostable packaging buy it through a channel BioPak already owns.

members: event and facilities-management suppliers bundling packaging into a contract
tier_4_adjacent_crossover.why: Procurement is bundled, so packaging is often decided by whoever supplies the wider contract.

members: sustainability consultants who specify a packaging standard
tier_5_professional_route.why: A consultant can mandate a certification that pre-selects a supplier.

members: government EPR and Green Plan 2030 pressure changing the default
tier_6_indirect.why: Regulation and reuse schemes can shrink the disposables category itself.

_expected.why: Fringe, sub-1% share against a verified structural incumbent. The category is real and growing (regulation is forcing adoption) but the position is not held: no recognition against BioPak, and the owner's own distribution is thin. Market headroom is genuinely present - that is the one favourable dimension - which is exactly the trap the report must not let mask the rest.
